extracted.intended_audience: GCC policymakers, national IP offices, legislators, enforcement bodies, and IP professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for reforming and strengthening patent systems, patent office practices, enforcement, and related IP institutions across GCC countries, drawing on EU practices and international agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope of patents for new uses of known products
rubrics_metrics.description: Oman to revisit its patent law in order to limit the scope of the provisions that extend patent protection to 'any new uses for, or new methods of using, a known product, including new uses and new methods for the treatment of particular medical conditions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 53 and 54 of the EPC can serve as an example to re-formulate such provisions. When possible, TRIPS flexibilities can be used. This is intended to reduce harmful effects on the generic sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary protection certificates (SPCs) to mitigate harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Oman and Bahrain to benefit from the EU practice known as supplementary protection certificates to make their laws less harmful to their local industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt SPC-type mechanisms judiciously to balance innovation incentives and local industry needs; consider EU SPC practice as a model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align maintenance fee grace periods with TRIPS
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC countries, with the exception of Bahrain and Oman, to amend the grace period for the payment of the fees prescribed for the maintenance of industrial property rights to be in line with TRIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform national fee/payment rules so they do not conflict with TRIPS; harmonize across GCC to avoid inequities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of burden of proof for process patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE to provide for the reversal of the burden of proof in respect of process patents as required by Article 34 of TRIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend procedural/evidentiary rules to allow right holders to rely on reversal of burden where appropriate under TRIPS Article 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend compulsory licence rules to avoid discrimination against imports
rubrics_metrics.description: Qatar and the UAE which provide that importing the product is not considered a legitimate reason by the patent holder for not granting a compulsory license should amend their laws to bring them in line with TRIPS that prohibits the discrimination of patents as to whether products are imported or locally produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compulsory licensing provisions do not discriminate between imported and locally produced products; align statutory language with TRIPS non‑discrimination principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join Budapest Treaty for deposit of microorganisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Kuwait and the UAE are invited to join the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms for the Purposes of Patent Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accession facilitates international recognition of deposits required in many patent filings; recommended to simplify biotech patent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join Strasbourg Agreement on International Patent Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that all GCC countries join the Strasbourg Agreement Concerning the International Patent Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting a common IPC facilitates search/examination harmonization and international cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign validation agreement with the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that GCC countries sign a validation agreement between their patent offices and the European Patent Office (EPO) according to which European patents will have legal effect in GCC countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation agreements can extend EPO-granted patent effects to GCC jurisdictions, reducing duplication of examination and creating efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt work-sharing modalities for patent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain GCC Patent Offices outsource the examination of their patent applications or collaborate with foreign experts. Modalities of work sharing that can be useful include Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH), PCT-PPH pilots, and SHARE (Strategic Handling of Application for Rapid Examination Project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PPH/PCT-PPH/SHARE to accelerate examination, improve quality, and leverage foreign office work; choose modalities appropriate to national capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate patents into innovation policy (standards, interoperability, competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision makers should pay more attention to the role of patents and their direct impact on the GCC markets. The relationship between digital technologies and patents should be at the core of their innovation policies, mainly issues relating to standardisation, interoperability, competition, patent licensing and open innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy assessments should evaluate how patent rules affect standard-setting, interoperability, competition law, licensing practices and open innovation; address these regionally given shared market effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building for patent professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC Patent Office to contribute to enhancement of current patent systems and the capacity building of patent professionals in patent drafting, patent litigation, patent commercialization, and transfer of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement training programs (e.g., EPO practice) targeting drafting quality, litigation strategy, commercialization and tech transfer skills to strengthen national patent ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support SMEs on IP usage and commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC Patent Office can help SMEs on how to use IP to protect and market their inventions, license their new technologies and attract investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance, outreach and possibly subsidized services to SMEs to increase IP uptake and commercialization; include practical advice on filing, licensing and investor pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize IP laws and policies regionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiate projects on regional collaboration among GCC countries such as harmonizing IP laws and policies, establishing a regional database for inventions and patents, and promoting technology transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional harmonization should focus on areas of common interest and economic benefit; use GCC Patent Office and specialized working groups to draft unified/regional instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a regional database for inventions and patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a regional database for inventions and patents for the benefits of the Arab countries by using the data for developing R&Ds in public institutions and universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create searchable, shared databases to support R&D, reduce duplication, and inform policy; ensure data governance and access rules are defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote technology cooperation and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting technology cooperation through technology transfer among GCC countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design programs and incentives for inter‑GCC licensing, joint R&D, and tech transfer mechanisms to increase regional innovation capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise public awareness on IP, inventions and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising awareness among the public on IP, inventions and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run targeted campaigns, integrate IP education into curricula, and tailor messages for different audiences to build an IP culture supportive of innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Launch regional projects on patents' market impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Launching regional projects on the role of patents and their direct impact on the GCC markets including the common market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct studies and pilot initiatives to understand how patent regimes affect competition, market structure, and innovation across the GCC common market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a regional professional body for patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a regional professional body for GCC patent agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a professional association to set standards, provide training, and professionalize patent agent practice regionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build judiciary capacity and court expertise on patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Building the capacity of the judiciary and court experts in the GCC on patent laws and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specialized training for judges and court experts; consider long-term programs (e.g., WIPO Academy) to develop IP judicial expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create specialized IP judges and courts carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC countries lack specialized IP judges. Restructuring the judicial system including establishment of specialized courts should be done after formation of a core group of specialized and competent national judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence reforms: first train and develop a core national judiciary with IP expertise, then consider specialized courts to ensure informed interpretation and timely decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create IP Unit within Customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each GCC country should have an IP Unit within Customs similar to units created by Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Main tasks: stop counterfeiting and piracy at the borders, monitor destruction of infringing goods and equipment used, coordinate with IP offices, establish common databases, cooperate with right holders and stakeholders, and exchange experience with other IP Units and task forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff units with trained officers and establish procedures for border measures, coordination with national IP offices, data sharing and stakeholder cooperation. Train officers via WCO, INTERPOL, Europol, OLAF on international best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train enforcement bodies and IP officers
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC countries should build the capacity of IP officers to have a knowledgeable and competent IP administrative body capable of managing efficiently IP offices including performing IP operations and examinations using best international practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train police, customs, sworn IP officers, prosecutors, judges, municipal officers and other enforcement bodies on IP principles, national laws, socio-economic impacts, and best practices for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide payment of legal costs by infringer
rubrics_metrics.description: All GCC countries to provide in their laws for the payment by the infringer of the legal costs as required by TRIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure statutes authorize recovery of legal costs from infringers to reduce enforcement barriers and align with TRIPS obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design targeted IP awareness campaigns and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising IP awareness through IP campaigns and trainings: address the right message to the right public (e.g., consumers should be informed about health/safety dangers of counterfeit products, link IP crimes to other crimes, inform about legal consequences, integrate IP into school curricula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design campaigns with IP experts, communication specialists and psychologists to understand consumer behavior; integrate long-term IP education strategies into school curricula at all levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create national IP task forces for coordinated enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a national IP task force for each GCC country composed of representatives of existing enforcement bodies (sworn IP officials, police and customs officials) to coordinate IP enforcement cases, conduct joint raids and enforce IP laws more efficiently, and collaborate regionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form multi-agency task forces with clear mandates, regular meetings, and mechanisms for regional collaboration and intelligence sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an IP Enforcement Portal for coordination and data
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC countries can join efforts to create an IP enforcement portal similar to the one created by the EUIPO to enhance national coordination between rights holders and enforcers, share information securely, collect enforcement data for analysis, and inform about third party infringements and GCC activities in IP crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a secure online platform for rights-holder notifications, enforcement case tracking, data collection and inter-agency coordination; ensure privacy and access controls.
